# Results -- Study 269 (Baltic-Dry) on the real monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: at each
month-end, compute the 3-month log change of the Baltic Dry Index (BDI) as a
momentum signal; (a) regress the *next* month's S&P 500 return on it (HAC t on
the slope is the inference bar), and (b) trade a long-when-BDI-rising overlay
(long the S&P next month if the signal is positive, else cash) against
buy-and-hold. One-month execution lag throughout; one-way costs on each switch.
**Curated BDI series**: the BDI is a licensed Baltic Exchange product with no
clean free feed, so the real tape pairs a curated monthly reconstruction of the
index (public waypoints, log-interpolated) with Shiller monthly S&P 500. The
turning points are chosen with hindsight -- real numbers are indicative, not a
live backtest of the official daily fixing. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint (last row) |
|--------|--------|-------|----------------------|
| Curated BDI (monthly) x Shiller S&P 500 (monthly nominal) | 1985-01-31 -> 2026-05-31 | 493 paired months | `754cb2059bb5` |

The BDRY dry-bulk freight ETF (inception 2018) is available as a tradable proxy
on `--fetch --proxy`, but only covers ~8 years -- too short for the headline run.

## Primary specification -- predictive regression

Regress next-month S&P 500 return on the 3-month BDI momentum signal:

| | Slope (beta) | HAC *t* | R^2 | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Full sample 1985-2026** | **+0.0310** | **+2.82** | 0.045 | 493 |
| **Ex-2008/09 crisis** | +0.0106 | **+1.35** | -- | 469 |

The full-sample slope clears *t* = 2 -- but it is **almost entirely the 2008-09
co-crash**: drop the 24 crisis months and the HAC *t* falls to **+1.35**, below
the inference bar. The BDI and equities both collapsed together in late 2008;
that single episode does most of the work. This is a fragile, regime-driven
"signal", not a stable lead-lag.

## Sub-period analysis -- the slope is not stable

| Period | Slope (beta) | HAC *t* | n |
|--------|------------|---------|---|
| 1985-1999 | **-0.0591** | -1.41 | 177 |
| 2000-2009 | +0.0541 | **+5.08** | 120 |
| 2010-2026 | +0.0190 | +2.28 | 196 |

The slope is **negative** in 1985-1999, large and significant only in the
commodity-supercycle + GFC decade (2000-2009), and modest afterward. A signal
whose sign flips across sub-periods is not a robust predictor.

## Tradability -- the timing overlay loses to buy-and-hold

Long the S&P next month when the BDI is rising, else hold cash (0%); 5 bps
one-way on each switch (only ~21 switches over 41 years -- turnover is trivial).

| Strategy | Return/yr | Ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* | Max DD |
|----------|-----------|-------------|---------|--------|
| Buy-and-hold S&P (price-only) | **+9.86%** | **+0.80** | +4.38 | -50.8% |
| Timing overlay (gross) | +6.62% | -- | -- | -- |
| Timing overlay (net, 5 bps) | +6.60% | +0.76 | +3.97 | -43.7% |
| **Timing - buy-and-hold** | **-3.26%** | -- | **-1.90** | -- |

The overlay sits in cash whenever the BDI is falling, which mostly means
**sitting out good equity months**: it gives up ~3.3%/yr versus simply staying
invested, and the underperformance is nearly significant on its own (*t* =
-1.90). The slightly shallower drawdown (-43.7% vs -50.8%) is the only crumb of
value, and it is not worth a third of the long-run equity premium. Price-only
returns (no dividends) on both legs, so the comparison is apples-to-apples.

## Sign hit-rate -- worse than the base rate

The sign of the BDI signal agrees with the sign of next month's S&P return only
**54.6%** of the time -- *below* the unconditional base rate of **64.7%** (the
market simply rises most months). Knowing the BDI direction makes you a *worse*
directional bettor than always saying "up".

## Positive control -- the machinery works when a lead-lag exists

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_series`), where next-month
equity returns are built to depend on this month's BDI change via a ``beta``
knob, the same regression recovers the planted slope monotonically:

| Planted beta | Estimated beta | HAC *t* | R^2 |
|--------------|----------------|---------|-----|
| 0.0 (null)   | -0.008         | -1.07   | 0.003 |
| 0.3          | +0.086         | +10.55  | 0.183 |
| 0.6          | +0.182         | +17.50  | 0.321 |

The engine reads ~zero on the null and lights up sharply when a real lead-lag is
planted -- so the weak, fragile reading on the real tape is a property of the
data, not a broken test harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** The full-sample regression slope clears *t* = 2 (+2.82),
  which would naively read REAL -- but it is driven almost entirely by the
  2008-09 co-crash (ex-crisis *t* = +1.35), the slope is *negative* in
  1985-1999, and the sign hit-rate (54.6%) is below the base rate (64.7%). A
  predictor that only "works" in one crisis decade and whose sign flips across
  sub-periods does not clear a *robust* inference bar. Add the curated-series
  caveat (hindsight waypoints flatter in-sample fit) and the honest grade is
  **WEAK**, not REAL.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The tradable read of the claim -- a
  long-when-BDI-rising overlay -- **loses 3.3%/yr to buy-and-hold** (*t* =
  -1.90) and delivers a lower Sharpe. The only benefit is a marginally shallower
  drawdown, nowhere near worth surrendering a third of the equity premium. There
  is no exploitable edge here. Verdict: **MIRAGE**.
- **Curated-series bias -- named.** The real BDI tape is a hindsight-curated
  monthly reconstruction; an in-sample fit is flattered. All real-tape numbers
  are indicative upper bounds on a live implementation of the official fixing.
